Admitting Officer
Emergency Department
Children’s Hospital
Newtown

18/01/2014
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Joshua Vance                        DOB 17/11/2013

I am writing to Joshua Vance, a 6-week-old male baby, whose clinical features are suggesting of              Commented [AH1]: refer
constipation with mild dehydration. Your urgent assessment would be highly appreciated.                      Commented [AH2]: suggestive

Joshua was born by normal vaginal delivery at the 38th week of gestation without any complications.
Moreover, his birth weight was 3250g.

On 31/12/2013, the baby was attended by his mother for the routine check-up. She worried about his           Commented [AH3]: presented
bowel action, as he defecated only once every 3 days, and his stool was hard. However, his examination       Commented [AH4]: a
was unremarkable. Consequently, the mother was reassured that her baby had only mild constipation, for       Commented [AH5]: was
which she was instructed to express milk from one feed a day and give it to the baby with some water. On     Commented [AH6]: start new paragraph
13/01/2014, regrettably, the condition did not improve. Furthermore, he suffered from sleeping
deprivation with excessive crying, and he frequently moved up his legs towards the chest and refused
feeding. His abdominal examination revealed only hard faeces. Accordingly, I prescribed Coloxyl drops.       Commented [AH7]: only revealed

Today, unfortunately, the condition was deteriorated, as the baby had not passed stool during the previous   Commented [AH8]: has
5 days. He also refused feeding and vomited once, only without passing urine. On examination, the baby       Commented [AH9]: a
was not only irritable but also showed signs of mild dehydration. Moreover, his abdominal examination
revealed diffuse tenderness without guarding or rebound tenderness.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor



                                     Report
 Word length                  243
 Comments                     The letter too long but overall well structured.
                              Difficulties with tenses, articles and active-passive
                              form are evident.
 Estimated Grade               B
 Advice                       1. Revise grammar.
                              2. Try to write no more than 200 words by
                                  planning paragraphs to focus on the most
                                  important parts of the case notes.
                              3. Always proofread the letter after finishing
                                  writing it.
